_how_to_fill: Fill each entry following references/writing-descriptions.md in the bi-joe-data-profiler skill. source: system_metadata | user_documentation | inferred | pending. When source is inferred, confidence (high|medium|low) and evidence are required. Put `backticks` only around real table names, column names or observed values. Suggest BEAM annotations in beam{} following references/beam-annotations-guide.md. Then run: bijoe check <dir> and bijoe render <dir>.

dataset.summary: Reference data for a shoe retailer trading as StepUp: the people who buy from it, what it sells, and where it sells. It holds no sales or other business events.
evidence: All 15 store names start with "StepUp" (checked separately)
Three sheets of customers, products and stores; none holds transactions

Customers.definition: A customer is a person who has made one or more purchases from the company, identified by `CustomerID`.
Customers.description: One row per customer, identified by `CustomerID`, with contact details, demographics and loyalty status (`LoyaltyTier`). Each customer has a home store in `PreferredStoreID`, and every value matches a `Stores.StoreID`. Sign-ups run from 2018-01-26 to 2026-09-17. `TotalOrders` and `LifetimeSpend` are totals stored per customer; with no order table in the workbook, they cannot be split by date, product or store.
evidence: `CustomerID` unique and never missing across 200 rows
`PreferredStoreID` has 15 distinct values, all found in `Stores.StoreID` (measured relationship)
`SignupDate` min 2018-01-26, max 2026-09-17
`TotalOrders` integer 1-40; `LifetimeSpend` decimal 32.68-3950.48
`LoyaltyTier` values: `Gold` (59), `Platinum` (49), `Bronze` (47), `Silver` (45)
`FirstName`, `LastName`, `BirthDate` and `Gender` (`M`, `F`, `Other`) describe people
`TotalOrders` minimum is 1
open_questions: On what date were `TotalOrders` and `LifetimeSpend` last calculated?
Does `LifetimeSpend` include tax and returns, and what currency is it in?
`Seattle` is the most common customer city (27) but has no store. Are these online customers?

beam.table_why: One row per `CustomerID` (unique in all 200 rows), with descriptive columns and no validity dates, version numbers or current-flag columns, so the sheet holds only current values.

CustomerID.why: The source's own identifier for each customer: unique, never missing, `C00001`-style codes.

BirthDate.why: A person's date of birth should not change; corrections overwrite it.

SignupDate.why: Signing up happens once, so the date should not change.

LoyaltyTier.why: Four tiers (`Gold`, `Platinum`, `Bronze`, `Silver`): the main way to segment customers in a dashboard.

PreferredStoreID.why: Plays the role of 'preferred store' of the `Stores` dimension; every value matches `Stores.StoreID`.

TotalOrders.why: A count that sums correctly across customers, but it is a stored total, not individual orders, and its as-of date is unknown.

LifetimeSpend.why: An amount that sums across customers. A stored total whose currency, as-of date and treatment of tax and returns are unknown.

Products.definition: A product is a shoe model in one colour that the company sells or has sold, identified by `ProductID` and `SKU`.
Products.description: One row per product, identified by `ProductID` and a unique `SKU`, covering 8 brands and 8 categories. `UnitPrice` is above `UnitCost` for every product, so margin can be calculated per product. Product names are not unique: `Velora Glide Boots` is three products in different colours, so count and filter by `ProductID`, not by name.
evidence: `ProductID` and `SKU` both unique and never missing across 60 rows
`Brand` 8 distinct values, `Category` 8 distinct values
`UnitPrice` > `UnitCost` in all 60 rows (checked separately); price 22.99-227.99, cost 8.23-117.92
`ProductName` 58 distinct in 60 rows; `Velora Glide Boots` appears 3 times (Grey, Green, Blue)
Each row has one `Color`; `Velora Glide Boots` exists as three products in different colours
`IsActive` is `False` for 6 products
open_questions: One active product has a `LaunchDate` of 2026-11-19, after the profile date. Is that a planned launch or an error?
Should inactive products (`IsActive` = `False`, 6 products) appear in reports?
What currency are `UnitPrice` and `UnitCost` in, and is `UnitPrice` before or after tax?

beam.table_why: One row per `ProductID` (unique in all 60 rows), with descriptive attributes and no validity dates or version columns.

ProductID.why: The source's identifier for each product: unique, never missing, `P0001`-style codes.

SKU.why: Unique `SKU-639131`-style codes; a SKU is the identifier people use on shelves and boxes.

Category.why: Eight categories: the natural first grouping for product dashboards.

UnitPrice.why: A unit price can't be summed; use average, min or max. Its currency is unknown.

UnitCost.why: A cost per unit can't be summed, for the same reason as the price.

StockQty.why: A stock level: it can be summed across products, but not over time.

LaunchDate.why: A launch date should not change, but one value lies in the future.

Stores.definition: A store is a physical StepUp shop (an outlet, flagship, kiosk or standard store), identified by `StoreID`.
Stores.description: One row per store, identified by `StoreID`, with location, manager, size and `StoreType` (`Outlet`, `Flagship`, `Kiosk` or `Standard`). Stores opened between 2010-10-14 and 2024-02-28, in 9 cities across 8 states, and every store is the preferred store of at least one customer. Two different stores share the name `StepUp Northpoint Houston` (an outlet and a standard store at different addresses), so label stores by `StoreID`, or by name plus address.
evidence: `StoreID` unique and never missing across 15 rows
`City` 9 distinct, `State` 8 distinct
`StoreType` values: `Outlet` (6), `Flagship` (4), `Kiosk` (3), `Standard` (2)
`StoreName` 14 distinct in 15 rows; S007 and S008 share a name (checked separately)
All 15 `StoreID` values appear in `Customers.PreferredStoreID` (measured relationship)
Every store has an address, `SquareFeet` and `Employees`, so it is a physical location
open_questions: Is the shared `StoreName` `StepUp Northpoint Houston` intentional (two stores in one mall) or a data entry error?

beam.table_why: One row per `StoreID` (unique in all 15 rows), with descriptive attributes and no validity dates or version columns.

StoreID.why: The source's identifier for each store, S001 to S015, and the target of `Customers.PreferredStoreID`.

StoreName.why: Not unique: two different stores share one name.

StoreType.why: Four store formats (`Outlet`, `Flagship`, `Kiosk`, `Standard`): a natural way to compare stores.

OpenDate.why: A store opens once, so the date should not change.

SquareFeet.why: The column name states the unit.
